## Definitions

- [statement] An expiry label is an event category, not proof of zero economic P&L: Hudson & Thames assign expiry a neutral class, while the triple_barrier repository specifies a market-price convention for expiry. Preserve expiry price and net return separately. (medium confidence) — https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] A generic triple-barrier package is not by itself a cost-complete execution simulator. The mchiuminatto labeler README lists tick-data support and trading costs among future work and warns that the library has not been tested for real trading. Verify those omissions before using its labels as executable SOL outcomes. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Historical parameter recommendations are not current configuration: the June recommendation and the later July recommendation use different SOL imbalance thresholds. Read the custody state for each simulated trade. (medium confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/price-impact-parameter-recommendations-june-3rd-2025/38497 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://discuss.jup.ag/t/trading-volume-analysis-and-price-impact-parameter-updates/39189, https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/technical-reference.md
- [statement] The July historical analysis refers to a ten-minute imbalance window, while Jupiter’s later fee documentation says roughly the last minute. Treat the window as a version-dependent assumption that needs onchain validation. (low confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/trading-volume-analysis-and-price-impact-parameter-updates/39189 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] HFT Architecture warns that exchange clocks are not synchronized. A SOL lead measured from exchange timestamps therefore needs clock-offset checks before it is interpreted as an available trading window. ## Structure and components

- [statement] Research proposal, not an observed result: test a shared representation with a SOL-specific component against both full pooling and SOL-only estimation. Pindza supplies a simple hierarchical baseline and evidence of asset heterogeneity; Fused Encoder Networks supplies an example that retains a separate target encoder. Neither source validates this proposed combination for five-minute SOL perpetuals. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3
- [statement] Pindza’s transfer finding is bounded by bar-derived microstructure proxies, a short historical window and one exchange. The author explicitly says the results may not generalise to other exchanges and that cross-exchange arbitrage dynamics are absent; this prevents treating the transfer matrix as universal market structure. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] For this five-minute study, use a five-minute wall-clock expiry as a design choice. On irregular event bars, a fixed bar count does not preserve a fixed elapsed-time horizon. This is a labeling specification, not evidence of profitability at that horizon. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The JLP liquidation boundary is fee-dependent: the documented long and short formulas deduct close fees and accumulated borrow fees from recorded collateral. Borrow fees can move the boundary while the trade remains open. A fixed adverse-price percentage therefore omits part of the documented mechanism. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Bayesian Market Filters page contains conflicting descriptions: its repository description advertises walk-forward validation, while the audited README says the models were fitted once and frozen. The audit also says that unsupported passive fills and execution delay undermine the reported positive results; treat this as implementation evidence, not a validated trading edge. (low confidence) — https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival

## How it works

- [statement] Pindza’s hierarchical linear model pools feature effects across assets and uses an asset random intercept; it estimates on a random subsample for tractability. This is partial pooling of baseline returns, not evidence that every asset shares an identical predictive mechanism. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] OHLC data can leave the first exit unidentified when both barriers lie inside one bar. ML4T resolves that case as stop loss, and a cited backtesting issue participant recommends the same pessimistic convention. This is an assumption about an unknown path, not an observed order of events; retain an ambiguity flag. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/kernc/backtesting.py/issues/1224
- [statement] Zollo and colleagues propose jointly optimizing an acceptance model and a recalibrator so that the retained region is easier to calibrate. This is a candidate design for an abstaining signal system, not a demonstrated five-minute SOL result. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05407v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] A trade that reduces recent imbalance incurs no additive fee, even if imbalance remains above threshold. A worsening or sign-flipping trade can incur it above threshold; liquidations contribute to the flow state but never pay the additive fee themselves. Entry and exit therefore need separate fee calculations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Gauntlet and Chaos Labs both reported trade splitting under the earlier size-only mechanism. The additive model was designed to address that weakness; those observations do not demonstrate current five-minute trader profitability. (medium confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/gauntlet-comprehensive-analysis-jupiter-perpetuals-price-impact-structure-implementation-and-proposed-adjustments/19127 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://discuss.jup.ag/t/chaos-labs-jupiter-price-impact-fee-mechanism-review/19969, https://discuss.jup.ag/t/additive-on-imbalance-price-impact-model/38562
- [statement] For a reproducible feasibility test, save contemporaneous custody parameters and the recent flow state. The documented fields include pricing.tradeImpactFeeScalar, priceImpactBuffer.deltaImbalanceThresholdDecimal, jumpRateState, increasePositionBps and decreasePositionBps. Thresholds, rounding and borrow-rate state must be replayed for each side; this is a research-method recommendation, not a claim that a historical state archive is available. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/technical-reference.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] The negation evidence scopes the claim that high volume necessarily causes high impact fees: Chaos Labs’ 2024 review says offsetting buy/sell trades can keep delta imbalance small, while informed traders trading before alpha decays can face costs that splitting does not avoid. Its historical simulations and proposed parameters should not be presented as present-day measured execution costs. (low confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/chaos-labs-jupiter-price-impact-fee-mechanism-review/19969 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] In the cryptocurrency volatility study, statistical significance changed with the chosen Markov order and could disappear at higher orders. The reported information-flow results also depend on binning and source/target block lengths. Lag and discretization sensitivity therefore belong in an uncertainty audit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9601717/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Historical crypto information-flow direction should not be assumed permanent. Keskin and Aste explicitly warn that causation varied within their sample and that persistence is unproven; the daily-price leadership study likewise reports no definite information-transfer leader in its studied market. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8624574/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] JLP-market cost modeling must include base fees and linear plus additive price impact on both entry and exit. Jupiter documents a 0.06% base fee per side; these rules are distinct from Beta markets, which use maker/taker fees and hourly funding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] HFT Architecture reports that KuCoin ranked ahead of Binance in SOL perpetual price leadership on both exchange and Tokyo receipt clocks in its July 2026 sample. The author limits the leadership conclusion to 10–700 ms. This is one vendor study, not independently replicated SOL execution evidence. (low confidence) — https://hftarchitecture.com/insights/crypto-exchange-lead-lag · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In Pindza’s five-minute forward-return experiment, which includes Solana, models trained on one cryptocurrency fail to transfer to other cryptocurrencies. Treat this as a result for this dataset and model pipeline, not an impossibility theorem. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Negation evidence: Lima’s equity-factor case-study abstract reports that learning triple-barrier targets can fail economically when translated into a portfolio. This scopes label-based claims; it is not a SOL-perpetual experiment. (low confidence) — https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7177958 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Probability calibration and useful abstention are distinct objectives. Zhu and colleagues report calibration methods that harm error detection in image classifiers; the ICLR blog explains that calibration alone does not establish useful decisions for individual inputs. This is a warning against treating a calibration improvement as proof of better signal selection. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02970 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://iclr-blogposts.github.io/2026/blog/2026/useful-calibrated-uncertainties/
- [statement] A risk-coverage curve evaluates selection by pairing the error or loss among accepted predictions with the fraction of predictions accepted. It answers a different question from whether a reported probability matches an observed frequency. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02970 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Farinhas and colleagues propose non-exchangeable conformal risk control for the expected value of monotone losses. The framework weights observations by relevance to a test example. This is a candidate method for dependent or drifting data, subject to its loss and bound assumptions. (low confidence) — https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/de04896f011beff76c91e094f72727f4-Abstract-Conference.html · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Selective prediction evaluates a predictor together with an acceptance rule. Coverage is the probability of acceptance; selective risk is expected loss conditional on acceptance. For a five-minute signal, using these as an evaluation framework is a proposed application, not evidence of trading performance. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12084v2 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Calibration quality and selective accuracy are separate objectives. Zhu and colleagues report that many calibration methods worsen error detection in their experiments; Zollo and colleagues note that enforcing selective calibration can decrease accuracy. Consequently, lower calibration error alone should not be used as evidence of a better acceptance policy. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2303.02970v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05407v1
- [statement] The Zhou–Wang audit conditions its selective-risk certificate on exchangeable calibration and test points. It also states that its conservative per-group mitigation has no formal guarantee for unseen groups. Applying that certificate to chronologically deployed SOL signals would require a separate justification of its assumptions. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2606.15153v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Methodological inference from conditional selective risk: evaluate net outcomes within the accepted population and report acceptance coverage. An average over all observation times alone does not determine the selected subset’s mean, so it cannot by itself rule out or establish the profitability of a rare-trigger policy. This is a distinction between conditional and unconditional evaluation, not a claim that any SOL policy is profitable. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12084v2 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Pindza reports severe regime dependence for the LightGBM model in a study targeting five-minute forward returns: apparent predictive content concentrates in calm, trending markets and disappears during stress. This is a study-specific warning, not proof that a volatility filter creates profitable SOL trades. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Methodological inference: compare any volatility-conditioned selector with a static baseline using chronological, purged walk-forward evaluation, and report stress-regime performance separately. RegimeNAS supplies the adaptive design precedent, while the Frontiers study shows why pooled performance and unpurged evaluation can conceal regime-dependent failure. This is a proposed evaluation design, not demonstrated SOL profitability. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full
- [statement] Chaos Labs designed the additive mechanism to resist order splitting and warned that even a small trade can incur higher fees in a highly imbalanced window. Jupiter documents that all trades, including the trader’s own and liquidations, enter recent flow; splitting within the same minute does not avoid the fee. Small order size alone therefore cannot establish low-cost feasibility. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/additive-on-imbalance-price-impact-model/38562 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] Glassnode states that its public-endpoint latency measurements do not predict end-to-end order execution time. Such measurements cannot, by themselves, specify the fill delay for a SOL cross-venue strategy. (low confidence) — https://latency.glassnode.com/cex/about · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The deep-fusion study symmetrizes its directed adjacency matrix before embedding. Proposed implication: preserve the original directed graph separately when the task needs a leader-to-follower direction; symmetric asset similarity alone cannot retain that direction. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02040 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Verbii and colleagues study source selection for five-day cryptocurrency volatility. Their finding that marginal distribution similarity need not select the best source is a useful hypothesis for source selection, but the forecast target and horizon differ from five-minute SOL returns. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35314 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Poh and colleagues propose Fused Encoder Networks with separate source and target modules and report favorable cryptocurrency momentum results. This is evidence that transfer can work in another financial task, rather than confirmation of five-minute SOL microstructure transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09968 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] In Pindza’s zero-shot LightGBM transfer experiment, transfer correlations are lower across cryptocurrencies than between the same cryptocurrency’s spot and futures markets. Treat this as evidence against assuming universal five-minute microstructure transfer, rather than a theorem excluding all transfer methods. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Poh, Roberts and Zohren provide a concrete transfer architecture: Fused Encoder Networks run a pretrained source encoder alongside a target encoder and concatenate their outputs. Their empirical use-case is weekly crypto momentum with foreign-exchange source data, so the architecture is a candidate mechanism rather than direct five-minute SOL evidence. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Triple-barrier labels describe the return path through profit-taking, stop-loss and expiry barriers, rather than only the direction at the next close. (medium confidence) — https://hudsonthames.org/does-meta-labeling-add-to-signal-efficacy-triple-barrier-method/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] First-passage labeling closes the hypothetical trade at the earliest profit target, stop loss, or expiry, rather than deciding its outcome only from the terminal price. Record the closing reason and time. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/mchiuminatto/triple_barrier
- [statement] A profitable barrier label should mean profit after the modeled costs, rather than merely a favorable price touch. ML4T recommends barriers above expected round-trip costs; Jupiter separately charges opening and closing costs and accrues borrow fees while a position is open. Use position-specific realized net cash flows for the outcome. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] A barrier level is not always an achievable fill: ML4T documents gap handling that exits at the opening price when the open has passed a barrier. Apply this distinction when calculating the loss rather than clipping all losses to the stop threshold. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ml4t/engineer/blob/main/docs/user-guide/labeling.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Zollo and colleagues state that selective calibration is not monotonic as individual examples are removed, and that a mismatch between training and deployment coverage can hurt test performance. A stricter acceptance threshold should therefore be evaluated at its actual coverage rather than assumed to improve calibration. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05407v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Pindza defines the descriptive volatility regimes by realized volatility relative to its sample median and reports higher spread proxies, trade intensity, and depth imbalance in the high-volatility regime. The paper describes a range-based spread proxy rather than measured executable bid-ask quotes. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Bayesian Market Filters repository provides a concrete causal regime-estimation pattern: fit a two-state HMM on the initial training data and use forward filtering probabilities rather than smoothed probabilities during the backtest. Its data and backtest are hourly BTC, not five-minute SOL. (low confidence) — https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] RegimeNAS provides a candidate selector architecture: regime probabilities condition the weighting or selection of specialized modules. This is a model design precedent, rather than an executable five-minute SOL result. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Zhivkov and Kandilarov report complete TEMA-BTC testing failure across all optimizers. Their experiment uses an hourly timeframe, includes SOL among the tested assets, assumes zero transaction costs, and has a single-run exploratory design; it provides adjacent evidence of strategy breakdown rather than five-minute SOL validation. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/5/761 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The documented linear impact rate rounds upward to whole basis points, with a 0.01% minimum, in addition to a 0.06% base fee when opening or closing a position. A small position is therefore not exempt from per-side trading costs; borrow, swaps and network charges remain separate. A round-trip or collateral-percentage calculation must state its entry and exit notionals and leverage assumptions; it is a calculation rather than a measured trading result. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The additive-fee state is recent net long-minus-short trade flow over roughly a minute, not total open-interest imbalance. Long opens and short closes increase it; short opens and long closes decrease it. The model should reconstruct this state at each execution rather than use a five-minute candle or aggregate open interest as its substitute. The reconstruction requirement is an inference from the documented mechanism. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/technical-reference.md
- [statement] Jupiter documents a 0.50% cap on base plus linear plus additive trading fees per side, rather than on every fee a trader can pay. Borrow, conditional collateral swaps and transaction charges are separate costs; treating 0.50% as an all-in round-trip ceiling would understate costs. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Collateral swaps are conditional costs: an input token differing from underlying collateral or an exit payout in another token can require a swap. Jupiter documents pool-weight adjustments to swap fees and use of the maximum input/output asset fee. Model these cash flows separately from notional trading fees instead of automatically adding the same swap percentage to every trade. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Methodological inference: test a candidate SOL venue signal against executable prices after measured decision-to-fill delay and trading costs, rather than crediting the full observed lead as available profit. HFT Architecture separates prediction from execution latency, spread and fees; Glassnode separates endpoint timing from execution timing. (medium confidence) — https://hftarchitecture.com/insights/crypto-exchange-lead-lag · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://latency.glassnode.com/cex/about
- [statement] García-Medina and Hernández warn that general transfer-entropy causality analysis can produce spurious links through indirect effects or shared drivers. Proposed implication: require conditional rather than merely pairwise evidence for a claimed leader. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Keskin and Aste found that adding histogram bins amplified both signal and noise. In their cryptocurrency sentiment analysis, quantile bins reduced the odd-versus-even bin sensitivity seen with equal-width bins; this is a study-specific estimation result rather than a universal bin-count rule. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The multivariate cryptocurrency-network authors restrict their conclusions to hourly observations and describe their CoinMarketCap weighted, non-traded-price study as explanatory rather than predictive. These findings are not a direct validation of executable five-minute SOL forecasts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Pindza’s MAML exercise uses a linear base learner with one task-specific gradient step. The author describes it as a feature-importance and robustness check, so its presence does not demonstrate a profitable adapted SOL trading strategy. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Bieganowski and Ślepaczuk report similar feature importance and SHAP shapes across cryptocurrencies. Their prediction target is a three-second mid-price return; this supports investigating reusable features, but does not establish five-minute cross-asset weight transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2602.00776v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Wang and colleagues describe negative transfer as a less related source hurting target performance and propose filtering unrelated source data. This provides a general methodological reason to test target-only baselines; it is not crypto-specific validation. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.09751 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Janus README describes five-minute multi-asset pretraining followed by thirty-minute supervised fine-tuning. That documented pipeline is an implementation lead, not validation of a five-minute SOL deployment. (low confidence) — https://github.com/aurumco/janus · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The arXiv record marks Hierarchical Projection for Adaptive Knowledge Transfer as withdrawn and states that a proof mistake needs revision. Exclude it as affirmative evidence that hierarchical transfer works. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-28) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08691 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Pindza studies the five-minute forward log return using minute-level Binance spot and perpetual-futures data for six cryptocurrencies, including Solana, over August 2025–February 2026. This is direct horizon evidence, restricted to that historical sample. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Fused Encoder Networks paper reports stronger crypto momentum performance than its benchmarks, but its weekly rebalancing and weekly data prevent interpreting that result as demonstrated five-minute transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2208.09968v3 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Verbii, Killinkarov and Yafarov report that distant-source selection can outperform nearest-source selection for some learner families, and that forward pilot selection improves on random transfer. Their task is five-day crypto volatility; they explicitly restrict the findings to an exploratory historical panel. This scopes any claim that marginal source similarity alone determines useful transfer. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35314v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Methodological inference for the SOL experiment: compare transferred or pooled models against a SOL-only model under the same chronological test boundaries, and select source assets using earlier target validation data. Pindza’s weak cross-asset results and Verbii et al.’s target-only, self-continuation and forward-pilot controls motivate this comparison; they do not establish its SOL performance. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35314v1
- [statement] Same-candle stop-loss and take-profit touches do not establish their execution order. A cited backtesting issue discusses pessimistic stop-first handling; QuantConnect staff recommend higher-resolution data for a backtest that executes both exits. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/kernc/backtesting.py/issues/1224 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://www.quantconnect.com/forum/discussion/8190/the-backtesting-executes-both-the-stop-loss-and-the-take-profit-on-the-same-trade/
- [statement] For Jupiter JLP-market labels, liquidation must use the oracle path and a changing liquidation boundary; a stop-loss does not guarantee execution before liquidation. This is venue-specific documentation, not a demonstrated five-minute survival rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Methodological inference: evaluate a five-minute barrier outcome together with realized net P&L after opening, holding and closing costs. A touched profit barrier alone does not establish an economically profitable execution. (medium confidence) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w
- [statement] The crypto triple-barrier study leaves detailed order-book slippage simulation outside its scope; its results therefore do not establish executable five-minute high-leverage SOL profitability. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Under the cited Jupiter JLP liquidation documentation, liquidation follows the oracle price, not a generic exchange candle. Liquidation consumes all remaining collateral after losses and applicable fees; model it as an absorbing exit before any later recovery. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] A stop price must not be treated as guaranteed survival. Jupiter warns that liquidation may occur before a stop executes; it also documents that submission and execution prices can differ, and excessive slippage can cancel a trade. Replay actual execution outcomes or state the execution assumption explicitly. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-07) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/positions-and-collateral.md
- [statement] The cited cryptocurrency study benchmarks triple-barrier labels against next-bar labels, but its transaction-cost experiment does not model slippage dynamically and uses one open transaction at a time. Its reported setup does not establish executable, high-leverage SOL performance at a five-minute horizon. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40854-025-00866-w · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Selective calibration evaluates whether predicted probabilities match outcome frequencies within the accepted subset. Fisch and colleagues train a separate selector for this objective; their author implementation describes the same accepted-population target. For the proposed signal gate, this motivates checking calibration after acceptance as well as before it. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12084 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/ajfisch/calibrated-selective-classification, https://arxiv.org/html/2208.12084v2, https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05407v1
- [statement] Adaptive conformal inference targets prediction-set coverage frequency over long time intervals under changing distributions. Gibbs and Candès subsequently adapt the update step size and obtain regret control over local intervals. These are online coverage objectives; interpreting them as a calibrated probability for each individual trade would exceed the stated guarantees. (medium confidence) — https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/hash/0d441de75945e5acbc865406fc9a2559-Abstract.html · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://jmlr.org/papers/v25/22-1218.html
- [statement] CAP constructs a calibration set using an adaptive pick on historical observations after a current observation is selected. Its dynamic extension targets long-run false coverage-statement rate, the overall miscoverage level of reported prediction intervals. (low confidence) — https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v26/24-0452.html · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The selective-prediction repository explicitly warns that choosing and evaluating its acceptance threshold on the same observations makes its reported coverage optimistic. Its documented remedy is a held-out split. For a five-minute signal study, this supports separating gate selection from final evaluation; it does not establish a trading threshold. (low confidence) — https://github.com/Kric123/selective-prediction · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The author repository documents an implementation of calibrated selective classification that learns a selector for calibrated uncertainty on accepted examples. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ajfisch/calibrated-selective-classification · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Zollo and colleagues evaluate selective recalibration on medical diagnosis and image classification. Their reported improvements provide evidence for those experiments; five-minute SOL performance remains an untested application in this evidence set. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05407v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Implementation recommendation: estimate a regime threshold from training or past observations, then apply it forward; do not turn a full-sample descriptive median into a live historical trading filter. Pindza supplies a sample-median regime description, while the Bayesian Market Filters implementation explicitly uses forward probabilities and trains its regime model only on the initial sample. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters
- [statement] Wen and coauthors report that intraday momentum and reversal patterns change with price jumps, announcement events, and liquidity. Their study uses hourly cryptocurrency data, so it motivates conditional signal selection without validating a five-minute SOL decision rule. (low confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1062940822000833 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Crypto quant research README lists a momentum strategy with a volatility-regime filter as a candidate requiring a fresh precommitted hypothesis. That statement is a research proposal, not a successful test of regime-conditioned signal selection. (low confidence) — https://github.com/anthonychungwork-byte/crypto_quant_research · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The intraday forecasting-horizon study explicitly distinguishes variability across repeated model runs from uncertainty due to temporal dependence and changing regimes, and calls for rolling-window or block-bootstrap intervals. Repeated-seed standard deviations therefore should not be read as evidence that a selected regime strategy generalizes across market conditions. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/applied-mathematics-and-statistics/articles/10.3389/fams.2026.1888767/full · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] RegimeNAS evaluated daily cryptocurrency OHLCV data. Its reported forecast improvements therefore do not directly validate a five-minute SOL signal selector; testing that transfer remains necessary. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] For JLP SOL, the documented base charge applies on both opening and closing, and the linear impact rate rounds upward. A base-fee-only backtest understates even small-trade costs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/julianfssen/jupiter-perps-anchor-idl-parsing/blob/main/src/examples/price-impact-fee.ts
- [statement] Borrow accrues continuously on full notional. A short holding period reduces accrual but does not remove it; conditional swaps and network costs also belong in the feasibility hurdle. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Feasibility inference: replay fee state at execution and model exit costs separately. Jupiter documents keeper fulfillment and a separate single-transaction path, so submission time alone does not establish a live position. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/technical-reference.md · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] In its July historical analysis, Chaos Labs reported lower SOL volume after the June fee update and explicitly warned that other factors could explain the association. This scopes claims that dynamic fees leave trading activity unaffected. (low confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/trading-volume-analysis-and-price-impact-parameter-updates/39189 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] OpenJUP describes matching decoded entry events to preceding pool snapshots and later closes. This is a useful independent data-collection lead, but this pass recovered no populated trade rows and makes no performance claim from it. (low confidence) — https://www.openjup.com/flow-toxicity/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The older Chaos Labs proposal says a close pays only the base rate, whereas Jupiter’s later documentation applies linear impact on closing. These are attributed descriptions of different dated models, not interchangeable execution rules. (low confidence) — https://discuss.jup.ag/t/chaos-labs-jupiter-price-impact-fee-mechanism-review/19969 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees.md
- [statement] Borrow fees accrue continuously on full position size without compounding, with utilization-dependent rates. For a constant hourly rate, a five-minute hold costs one twelfth of that hourly rate times notional; if utilization changes, integrate the changing rate. This is a cost-model implication of the documented accrual rule, not an observed five-minute rate. - [statement] Gauntlet’s September 2024 analysis optimized impact scalars and also explored joint base-fee/scalar optimization against order-book conditions. It is historical calibration evidence, not proof of current custody settings or a profitable five-minute strategy. Treat this as a historical Bitcoin finding; SOL applicability requires separate measurement. - [statement] Albers and coauthors explicitly omit market impact and latency concerns from the discussed historical taker PnL calculation. That calculation is not direct evidence of performance after executable latency, and its Bitcoin setting does not establish a SOL effect. - [statement] The Cross-Exchange-Arbitrage-Engine README leaves its results section as a template awaiting real data output. Its description is a research design, not empirical evidence that a latency-adjusted SOL edge survives. - [statement] Divyasshree N’s working-paper description reports SOL DEX leadership over Binance with a 40-minute lead, using 1-minute OHLC observations from September 4-5, 2025. (low confidence) — https://zenodo.org/records/17085264 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] In Albers and colleagues’ historical Bitcoin study, the simple pairwise taker strategies all had negative PnL after default execution fees. This historical BTC result is counterevidence to treating statistical venue predictability alone as a profitable SOL trade. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09750 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Keskin and Aste assess crypto information-transfer results with shuffled-series permutation tests and Z-scores. Their PyCausality repository demonstrates nonlinear transfer entropy with shuffling and significance output; this is evidence about dependency detection, not a probability of a profitable SOL trade. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://github.com/ZacKeskin/PyCausality
- [statement] Keskin and Aste warn that overly fine histogram partitions bias transfer-entropy estimates in finite samples. Proposed implication: test binning sensitivity before using a nonlinear dependency score as a feature. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] A method called multivariate transfer entropy need not estimate nonlinear dependence: García-Medina and Hernández used jointly Gaussian conditional distributions, explicitly equivalent to linear Granger dependence. Their network findings therefore do not validate a nonlinear estimator. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/, https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.4514
- [statement] Schnoering and Inzirillo report cryptocurrency relationships at one-minute and five-minute sampling and describe the relationships as time varying. This is historical evidence of changing dependencies, not a verified present-day SOL forecast. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.02040 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The Kimchi-premium study warns that maximizing a transfer-entropy statistic across lags produces an upward-biased null maximum and optimistic significance. Proposed implication for a five-minute experiment: predefine the lag search and include lag selection in multiplicity control. Its empirical horizon is not a five-minute SOL validation. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/9/1501 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Bongiorno and Challet introduce time-shifted transfer entropy to locate information-transfer timescales, including where transfer peaks and disappears. Their stated application is stock-price ticks, so applying this method to SOL remains a research proposal. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.10173 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] Transfer entropy measures directional statistical dependence by asking whether source history reduces uncertainty about the target beyond the target's own history. It can represent nonlinear dependencies; a symmetric association measure alone does not establish a leader. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/nlin/0001042 · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] Raw histogram transfer entropy requires finite-sample uncertainty assessment: sparse counts and overly fine partitions can produce positive bias. A larger raw value alone is insufficient evidence of a stronger predictive relationship. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16215
- [statement] Effective transfer entropy subtracts a shuffled-series baseline from observed transfer entropy. This corrects an estimated null baseline; significance assessment additionally compares the observed value with the shuffled distribution. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8624574/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7540793/
- [statement] Bivariate transfer entropy can report an indirect link caused by a chain or a common driver. Conditional multivariate analysis evaluates a source in the context of other selected histories, but the conditioning set must be restricted to manage dimensionality. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
- [statement] The cryptocurrency multivariate-network study uses maximum-statistic tests for candidate selection, minimum-statistic tests to prune redundant sources, and an omnibus collective test. These are explicit controls for repeated comparisons; choosing the largest unadjusted pairwise statistic is not the procedure studied. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7517310/ · keywords: Five-minute high-leverage SOL perpetual signals: executable direction and adverse-path survival
